messages:
jordan: Heads-up — acme-corp reported a huge billing delta. Dashboard shows ~1.2M tokens for 2026-03-10 window, invoice charged ~2.4M. Customer says spike correlates with a deployment and many client timeouts. Suspect replayed requests causing double-metering.

sasha: ugh. do we have a request_id / sample timestamps from the customer or ledger lines? can you attach gateway logs? :eyes: 

jordan: I pulled a debug trace from the customer's support payloads and our gateway. snippets below.

jordan: customer curl they ran (note no idempotency header):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --max-time 30 \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-small", "input":"..."}'
```

jordan: gateway logs around the event (timestamps UTC):
```
2026-03-10T03:11:58Z ingress-gw request_id=rid-84211 src_ip=18.9.22.44 path=/v1/generate idempotency_key=-
2026-03-10T03:12:28Z backend response sent request_id=rid-84211 status=200 latency=30245ms tokens=512
2026-03-10T03:12:29Z ingress-gw request_id=rid-84213 src_ip=18.9.22.44 path=/v1/generate idempotency_key=-
2026-03-10T03:12:29Z routed to backend fallback model (client retry)
2026-03-10T03:12:59Z backend response sent request_id=rid-84213 status=200 latency=30120ms tokens=512
```

jordan: billing ledger entries (simplified):
```
2026-03-10T03:12:28Z ledger_line id=ll-9001 acct=acme tokens=512 source=request rid=rid-84211
2026-03-10T03:12:59Z ledger_line id=ll-9002 acct=acme tokens=512 source=request rid=rid-84213
```

sasha: so two successful completions ~31s apart for same client and same prompt. no idempotency header -> client retried after request timeout and gateway forwarded both. that matches double billing.

mike: billing side here — I queried invoice items and see both ledger lines consumed for invoice generation. we don't currently dedupe by similarity or IP. we dedupe only when idempotency_key is present and matched to a previous successful billed request. billing table sample query to surface duplicates:
```sql
SELECT acct, count(*) as hits, sum(tokens) as tokens, array_agg(request_id) as rids
FROM ledger_lines
WHERE acct = 'acme' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-03-10' AND '2026-03-11'
GROUP BY acct
HAVING count(*) > 1;
```

sasha: reproduction steps for eng:
1) run a long request (simulate 30s generation) without `Idempotency-Key`
2) client side `--max-time` or network cut causes client to retry immediately
3) ingress forwards both requests to backend; each produces tokens -> billing twice

sasha: quick mitigation: teach gateway to treat duplicate requests from same src IP + identical payload + recently completed request as idempotent no-op for billing OR reject second when no idempotency header with 409? Need legal on rejecting vs returning cached response.

jordan: customer wants credit. can we do a one-off reconciliation to mark ledger_line ll-9002 as refunded/credit? what's safe process here?

mike: we can issue a credit; recommend marking ledger_line metadata: "reconciled=true" and create a negative ledger_line referencing original id. i'll handle the accounting entry, but need approval from finance. tagging @finance-team.

billing-bot: Incident created: FIN-2026-0430 — Customer double-billed due to replayed requests. Assigned to finance@m.redwood. :rotating_light: 

sasha: long-term fix options:
- require/encourage `Idempotency-Key` for mutating endpoints and document prominently
- gateway-level lightweight request fingerprinting dedupe window (e.g., 60s) — compare body hash + auth token + src_ip
- billing-side reconciliation job to detect quick replays and flag for human review

mike: also note edge-case: clients behind NAT will share src_ip; use auth token + payload hash not IP as primary.

jordan: action items agreed:
- mike to issue credit for ll-9002 and record FIN ticket (in progress)
- sasha + eng-infra to prototype 60s fingerprint dedupe (PR draft) — sasha will drop design doc
- support to contact customer with explanation + ETA

sasha: quick design notes I'll include in doc:
```
Fingerprint := HMAC(secret, auth_token || body_hash)
store(Fingerprint, status=success, tokens, ttl=60s)
on new request: if Fingerprint exists and status=success -> return cached response or return 409 with details
```

jordan: customer updated: thanks for fast response, please apply credit ASAP. they also provided additional spike traces which I uploaded to the ticket.

mike: billing update: credit issued for ll-9002, invoice adjusted. FIN ticket FIN-2026-0430 updated.

sasha: I'll open a short RFC and link to this thread. assigning to eng-infra for implementation. :white_check_mark: 

jordan: thanks team. leaving this thread open for follow-ups, but customer has been credited and we have a mitigation plan.
